question: Does a population-level virtual-cell transition model help the agent choose measurements that separate competing mechanism hypotheses, compared with the current magnitude-ranked world model, with no world model, and with fixed and random policies?

source.folds: compounds.csv fold column of the frozen 24 h preparation (five skeleton-grouped folds)

state.unit: population of one well (line x time x compound x dose x replicate); never a cell trajectory

variables.rna_shift: measured: pseudobulk log1p(CP10K) shift against the pooled vehicle of the same line, time and replicate, 2473 frozen genes
variables.hallmark_activity: inferred from rna_shift (mean shift over MSigDB Hallmark members present)
variables.cell_cycle: inferred: Tirosh S and G2M module means per cell, summarised per well
variables.population_size: measured proxy: log2(cells recovered in the well / mean vehicle-well cells on the same plate)

classes.rule: first matching rule wins; skeleton units; a class enters a tier's hypothesis pool only above the tier's minimum

episode.held_out: every compound of a pool class, predicted from its own fold's training compounds only
episode.contrast: the compound's class against every other pool class of the tier; the two hypotheses are presented in a seeded random order
episode.stop: after the first mechanism elimination or when the budget is spent
episode.missing_or_failed_measurement: charged, returns quality_failed, never updates a mechanism belief

detection.statistic: Pearson correlation of the rep1 and rep2 shift vectors over the 2473 genes
detection.null: vehicle-well pseudo-conditions: one rep1 vehicle well and one rep2 vehicle well of the same line and time, each shifted against the pooled vehicle of the other wells of its replicate
detection.threshold: max(0.10, 0.99 quantile of the null for the same line and time)

validator.shared_axis: unit vector of the mean shift of all training compounds at the same line, time and dose
validator.similarity: cosine after projecting the shared axis out of both vectors; a class's score is the maximum over its training compounds whose own response is detected at that condition (templates)
validator.elimination: eliminate B in favour of A only if the profile is detected, A has a template and s_A >= floor, and either s_A - s_B >= margin or B has no template while at least two B training compounds were measured there and none was detected
validator.absence: an undetected response eliminates nothing; it is recorded as no_detectable_response at intervention-implementation scope, because a failed perturbation and a mechanism that is inert at that condition predict the same observation

calibration.procedure: per fold, inner leave-one-compound-out over training compounds, all pool-class pairs
calibration.choice: the grid point with the most correct eliminations whose wrong-elimination rate is at most the maximum; ties go to the larger margin, then the larger floor; if none qualifies the fold never eliminates

costs.basis: laboratory units; model and API spend excluded
costs.selector_scalar: turnaround days (exposure + readout); wells reported beside it

policies.random: uniform over unexecuted menu actions; 20 seeds averaged
policies.fixed: tier B: 10 uM in A549, then 10 uM in MCF7; tier A: 24 h 10 uM, then 72 h 10 uM
policies.cost_only: the repository selector without a world model: every action declares both hypotheses, so ties go to cost then identifier; identifiers are <line>|<hours, three digits>h|<dose, five digits>nM, so the tie-break starts at the lowest dose and the earliest time
policies.magnitude: current MAESTRO: the same selector with the virtual-cell tie-break |predicted transcript_shift_norm| from five nearest training structures (Tanimoto, log-dose interpolation); a 72 h query is refused as in the served rung
policies.separation: scenario cards from measured training references: per action and hypothesis, the leave-one-out outcome frequencies of that class's training compounds under the validator; detection_power = mean probability of a correct elimination; chosen by maestro.acquisition.select_expected_coverage with a per-step budget of 8 days (exactly one action); an action whose correct-elimination probability is zero distinguishes nothing, and if no action distinguishes anything the policy defers
policies.separation_permuted: control: separation with class labels permuted among training compounds (seeded)
policies.dyn_ref: separation for step 1; step 2 conditions each hypothesis's outcome frequencies on reference compounds whose step-1 outcome category (detected or not) matches the held-out compound's
policies.dyn_model: dyn_ref, except that when step 1 was detected but ambiguous the held-out compound's own step-2 profile is forecast by the best transition arm and the validator is applied to forecast plus resampled cross-validated residuals
policies.oracle: hindsight best sequence under the budget (utility, then cost)

llm_arms.episodes: one seeded decoy per held-out compound in each tier
llm_arms.deepseek_base: task, hypotheses, menu with costs and line descriptions, results so far; no cards
llm_arms.deepseek_cards_permuted: the same with cards from permuted-label references (non-biological control)
llm_arms.jev_cards: Jev choice over action identifiers with cards, 8 repeats; a stable modal choice (agreement >= 0.6) is executed, otherwise the separation action
llm_arms.authority: every arm's chosen action is executed and read by the same deterministic validator; no model output is evidence
llm_arms.repeatability: 30 first-step deepseek_cards decisions repeated three more times

T2_time.what: A549 72 h shift from the same compound and dose at 24 h

T3_dose.what: a dose's shift from the same compound's measured neighbouring doses, same line and time; 10 uM from lower doses is extrapolation and is reported separately

T4_context.what: a line's 24 h shift from the same compound and dose in another line

T5_branches.what: validator-outcome probabilities for a held-out compound at a condition, per hypothesis
T5_branches.metric: log loss and Brier score of the realised outcome under the true class

transition_tasks.metrics: cosine and gene-wise R^2 against zero on held-out conditions whose target response is detected; replicate ceiling; class of the nearest template from the forecast versus from the observation
transition_tasks.latent: PCA with 20 components fitted on training conditions only; MLP one hidden layer of 64 units, early stopping on an inner validation split

primary.P1: tier B, correct-decision rate at budget 2: separation minus magnitude
primary.P2: tier A, correct-decision rate at budget 2: dyn_ref minus magnitude, and dyn_ref minus fixed
primary.P3: T2: best learned arm minus persistence, mean cosine on held-out detected conditions
primary.P4: LLM episodes: deepseek_cards minus deepseek_base, correct-decision rate
primary.P5: T5: multi_branch minus single_mean log loss

secondary: utility and regret against the oracle
lab cost and days to the first mechanism elimination
calibration of predicted correct-elimination probability (ECE, 10 bins)
rate of 72 h choices after an undetected 24 h result
applicability refusals and the served-versus-refused error

promotion.scenario_cards: P1 interval excludes zero in favour of separation; separation's wrong-elimination rate no more than 0.02 above magnitude's; the permuted control does not reproduce the gain (its difference from magnitude has an interval containing zero or is smaller than separation's); predicted correct-elimination probability has ECE <= 0.10 where served
promotion.time_component: P2 interval excludes zero in favour of dyn_ref
promotion.learned_transition: P3 interval excludes zero in favour of the learned arm, and dyn_model beats dyn_ref on tier A utility
promotion.otherwise: record the negative result and keep the simpler method

case_study.question: Slow-acting epigenetic writer inhibitors (DNA methyltransferase: azacitidine, decitabine; PRC2/EZH2: tazemetostat, UNC1999, EED226) against 'the perturbation failed' in A549
anchors: At 24 h their A549 responses are weaker than HDAC inhibitors' at matched dose (replicate agreement and shift norm).
From 24 h to 72 h their response grows more than HDAC inhibitors' does (ratio of 72 h to 24 h shift norm, same dose).
DNA methyltransferase inhibitors at 72 h raise HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE relative to 24 h (viral-mimicry programme, Chiappinelli 2015; Roulois 2015).
case_study.reading: anchors are literature expectations checked against the data; a failed anchor is reported as failed
